column4: Brent sustained >$85 → jet fuel cost up → (a) marginal-carrier failure + capacity deletion on FL routes AND (b) airfare up → FL visitor arrivals fall / trip length shortens → FL tourism $ decline → hospitality employment + TDT receipts fall → compounds the Canadian-boycott $ hole in the SAME winter window
column5: Jet fuel is the largest single controllable cost for a low-cost carrier, and FL leisure routes are the thinnest-margin, most price-elastic segment in the domestic network. A sustained crude shock therefore hits FL capacity BEFORE it hits FL demand: the marginal carrier exits (deleting seats permanently) while surviving carriers raise fares (suppressing the price-elastic leisure traveller). ⚠️ PRECEDENT, NOT ANALOGY: Spirit Airlines liquidated 2026-05-02 holding 31.4% of FLL (11M pax 2024); JetBlue backfilled +75% departures so NET << GROSS — capacity deletion is real but partially offset, and the offset is what makes this a $-per-visitor story rather than a bodies story.
column6: ⚠️ REINFORCING AND MIS-TIMED: the energy shock and the Canadian air-capacity deletion land in the SAME winter 2026-27 window and act on the SAME thin FL leisure routes, so the two channels COMPOUND rather than add. Second loop: higher airfare pushes marginal snowbirds to drive or not travel, which shifts the mix toward shorter/cheaper stays — lowering $-per-visitor even where BODIES hold, the exact NV bodies-down/dollars-up pattern MARCO tracks as its leading template.
column7: Carrier capacity decisions are made on FORWARD schedules, so a fare/capacity response to a crude shock is committed 3-6 months ahead of the affected season — meaning the winter 2026-27 FL schedule is being set NOW, against a crude level that has been >$85 since 8/10.
